chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
If a man is unable to pray standing, he should pray sitting. If he cannot pray sitting, he should pray lying on his back, with his legs extended towards the Qibla, nodding with nods.
ai.seo_question: What is the order of prayer postures for someone who cannot stand?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* details the graduated flexibility in Salah postures, reflecting the Shia principle of removing hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) for the ill or weak. It specifies that when lying down, one should face the Qibla with legs extended and use head nodding (*ima'*) for recitation and actions, a practice supported by Shia jurists as the standard for those unable to sit or stand.
